data.name: Nerielle
data.long_meaning: Nerielle is derived from the Hebrew name Neriah, which means 'light of God'. In the Bible, Neriah was a scribe and a prince, a man of the Chaldeans who held a high position in King Jehoiakim's court. He is mentioned in Jeremiah 32:12, where he is described as a 'faithful man who stands before the Lord'.

in_hebrew.name: נֵרִיאֶל
in_hebrew.meaning: בת אור, רענן, נשמה, חיים, דמות
in_hebrew.long_meaning: נֵרִיאֶל שָׁם היא תַמְצֵא אֵשׁ וְאוֹר, כְּבוֹד וְיָשְׁרָה, רוֹחַ וְנֶשֶׁם, וְעֵינֵי אֵל, כִּכַּר צָמֵר, שָׁלֵם וְשָׁלֵם, שֵׁם קָדוֹשׁ, נִשְׁמַת אֵל, אֲבוֹד וְאָבֵד, חָכְמָה וְיָשְׁרָה, הַעוֹמֵד עַל יְהוָה, בְּחֹרֶב שֶׁקֶר, בְּצַדִּיקִים יִשְׁעֶלֶת, שָׁלֵם וְשָׁלֵם, שָׁרֵד וְפָל, צַדִּיק וְיָשְׁרָה

in_greek.name: Νεριέλλη
in_greek.long_meaning: Η Νεριέλλη είναι μια ονομασία που περιλαμβάνει την ιδέα της αθανασίας, της ανθούσας ψυχής, της ζωής και της μορφής. Με την ανάμνηση του Νεραίων, το όνομα συνδέεται με την αθανασία και την ισότητα. Οι εκκλησιαστικές παραδόσεις συνδέουν την ονομασία με την ιδέα της αθανάτου ψυχής.

in_latin.name: Neriella
in_latin.long_meaning: Neriella est nomen quod includit notionem immortalitatis, animi floris, vitae et formae. Cum memoria Neeraionis, nomen connectitur ad immortalitatem et aequalitatem. Ecclesiasticae traditiones Neriellam nominem connectunt ad notionem animae immortalis.

in_english.name: Nerielle

With the remembrance of Nerian, the name is connected to immortality and equality. historical_references.reference: The character Nerielle appears in the 13th century French apocryphal text 'The Golden Legend' as a virgin martyr. She is said to have been a noblewoman from Tarsus in Cilicia who converted to Christianity and was persecuted for her faith under the Roman emperor Diocletian. Her resistance to Roman persecution led to her martyrdom.

Another reference to Nerielle can be found in the 16th century Italian hagiography 'Acta Sanctorum' where she is mentioned as a martyr of the Roman persecutions under Diocletian. The text describes her as a noblewoman from Syria who, along with her husband and three sons, was martyred for refusing to offer sacrifice to the Roman gods.
